notes: Governing document: the NYU Faculty Handbook effective July 1, 2016 (2018_06; the 2018-02-20 title page, 2018_03, shows the same edition), with its web pages 2018_00 (Leave of Absence) and 2018_02 (Tenure Clock Stoppage), whose text matches the PDF. 2018_05 is the university-wide Workload Relief Policy page (effective 2006-09-27). 2018_03 is a title page (dating only) and 2018_04 the University Benefits page; neither holds leave policy. Tenured and tenure-track faculty are not unionised; no collective agreement applies.
Reference date 2018-02-26. All documents date from before it and none is superseded on it as far as the sources show.

Calendar: the handbook states a two-term (semester) teaching year ('the regular teaching year consists of two terms, beginning in early September and mid-January'; leave and relief are stated in semesters), with no length, so calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order.

Birth parent chain: paid maternity leave 6 weeks (c1), inside the workload-relief semester in which the childbirth disability leave is completed (c6, R3b); or, when the leave ends between semesters, maternity 6 -> workload relief in the following semester (c7, consecutive_after c1); or two half semesters of relief (c8, in_lieu_of c6/c7). FMLA 12 workweeks (c10) concurrent_with c1. Discretionary: illness/disability leave up to 6 months (c3) concurrent_with c1, with salary continuation (c4) within c3.

Non-birth parent chain: FMLA 12 workweeks (c10, unlinked for this role since c1 is birth-only); workload relief one semester (c6 or c7 or c8) if the primary caregiver (only one parent may be primary); unpaid personal leave for child care (c9) is general-purpose and counted in no figure.

No component is linked two ways: c1 carries only 'within c6'; c3 carries 'concurrent_with c1'; c4 'within c3'; c7 'consecutive_after c1' and 'in_lieu_of c6'; c8 'in_lieu_of c6, c7'; c10 'concurrent_with c1'.

Workload relief timing wording differs between the handbook ('or, in the case of the birth parent, the semester in which the birth takes place') and the policy page ('If the primary caregiver taking workload relief is the non-birth parent, only the latter two (2) situations are relevant'); the handbook web page 2018_00 has a third ordering. The policy page reads most coherently; the difference does not change the coded lengths.

Tenure clock: the workload relief policy page says stoppage 'may be granted', the handbook workload relief text says 'will be granted', and the handbook's Tenure Clock Stoppage section says it 'will be granted automatically' for a parent primarily responsible for a new child; the specific handbook section governs (source precedence).
Sabbatical leave (handbook) is a research leave and not a component; workload relief counts as sabbatical credit.

Documents cited but not saved: the Workload Relief Form / Workload Relief Application (PDF) and Workload Relief contact sheet; 'Your Rights under the Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993' (Benefits Office); the NYU long-term disability insurance plan and benefits booklets; school policies for Continuing Contract Faculty; the New York University Promotion and Tenure Guidelines; school statements on promotion and tenure.
This record also stands for NYU's Tandon School of Engineering (lead's version note); the handbook provisions are university-wide and no Tandon-only provision appears in the sources.
